question: The rate at which electrical energy is dissipated in an electric circuit is called ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric power**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** rate at which electrical energy is dissipated in an electric circuit is called electric powe**r.
 
• It is also the** rate at which electrical energy is consumed or supplied by an electrical component**
 
• Mathematically,

P = (W)/(t) = VI = {I²}R = frac{{{V²}}}{R}

 
• Where V = Potential difference, R = Resistance and I = current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Electric Work:

 
 
• The e**nergy transferred by an electric current in a circuit. **
 
• **It is done when charges move under the influence of an electric potential difference (voltage).**
 
 
 
• **Electric Heat**:
 
 
• The heat energy produced due to the flow of electric current through a conductor (due to resistance in the material).
 
 
 
• **Electric Force:**
 
 
• The force **exerted by charged particles on each other. **
 
• **It can be attractive or repulsive, depending on the nature of the char**ges.
